purpose: Evaluate the maintained Vercel agent-browser CLI as an isolated browser provider after Microsoft Playwright MCP and two maintenance candidates remained blocked by vulnerabilities.

functionalProof.fixture: A02 local form action with independent server oracle

positive: Upstream domain allowlisting was active in the closed cell.
Chrome binary is immutable outside the disposable user-home, socket, cache and profile tmpfs paths.
The candidate ran non-root with read-only rootfs, no Linux capabilities, no host mount, no published port and a gatewayless network.
notAdmissibleAsIs: The default MCP core profile includes JavaScript evaluation.
The package exposes plugins, saved browser state, credentials and a full tools profile.
Eva may therefore only use a future narrow adapter with fixed allowed domains and individually admitted action types; it may never hand the upstream full MCP tool surface to a model.

decision.reason: The provider passed the isolated functional cell but the same fresh advisory snapshot still reports 8 CRITICAL and 55 HIGH findings. Eva's release gate remains zero.
decision.next: Keep this as a concrete community-provider comparison. Do not deploy it; evaluate a materially cleaner maintained browser base or wait for upstream security fixes before repeating the exact cell.

nonclaims: This is not an Eva deployment, managed-B change, Telegram test, public account flow, download proof or human-takeover proof.
This does not modify Eva 1, its SQLite memory, its service, live credentials or volumes.
This does not make the upstream MCP core profile safe to expose directly to an Eva model.
